testDocs.title: Understanding Distributed Systems Consensus Algorithms
testDocs.content: Consensus in distributed systems is a fundamental problem that has been studied extensively. The Paxos algorithm, first described by Leslie Lamport, provides a way for distributed systems to reach consensus even in the presence of failures. Raft is a more understandable alternative to Paxos that achieves consensus through leader election. Both consensus algorithms ensure that distributed systems can maintain consistency across nodes. Distributed systems require consensus for fault tolerance and reliability.
